What kind of career path? · which job titles

Primary Product — core engineering roles

  • Process Engineer
  • Safety Engineer
  • Process Design / Selection
  • Production / Planner
  • Research & Development

Inside the process itself — refining, petrochemicals, food, pharma, energy

What kind of career path? · which job titles

Valuable by-Product — adjacent roles

  • Sale Engineer
  • Marketing
  • Finance / Risk evaluation
  • Start Up / BD

Same industry, but selling and deciding rather than running the unit

What kind of career path? · which job titles

Fuel — roles far from the process

  • Stock Trading
  • Financial Analyst
  • Financial Planner
  • Pilot
  • Entrepreneur
  • Start Up

Approved departmental elective · the registration rules

You may take more than six credits

Six credits are required Two courses from the list, or from any later department announcement
Extra courses still earn a letter grade A, B+, B, C+, C, D+, D, F — and they count toward your cumulative GPA
Which extras qualify ChemE electives (2105XXX) in the book or announced later · foreign-language courses · any Faculty of Engineering course (21XXXXX)
Anything else in the university Needs the curriculum committee's or the department committee's approval before you register
No approval, no grade Register over quota without approval and the committee changes the result to W
Your cohort: general education is S/U Gen-ed courses are graded satisfactory / unsatisfactory, so they cannot lift your GPA — the electives above can

Ask before you register, not after — the committee applies the Faculty announcement in force at the time

Preliminary chemical process synthesis · step 1 of 5

It starts with one reaction

A(l) + B(g)  →  C(g) + D(l) + E(l)
Reaction condition
Temperature90 °C
Pressure10 bar
Conversion100%
Phasesgas and liquid, over a packed solid catalyst
What comes out
Cgas by-product
Dliquid primary product — this is what you are selling
Eliquid by-product

Everything downstream — every pump, every column, every course — exists to get D out of that equation

Step 2 of 5

How do you separate it?

Phase Separator

Splits gas from liquid

C leaves as gas · D and E stay liquid

Inlet50 °C · 10 bar
Outletssame as inlet
→
Liquid Purifier

Splits D from E

Two liquids, one column

Inlet2 bar
Top50 °C · 2 bar
Bottom80 °C · 2 bar

Two decisions, and the shape of the whole plant is already fixed

Step 3 of 5 · block flow diagram

At first it is only a black box

Two feeds in, three streams out, every condition named — you can already write a mass and energy balance across this box

Step 4 of 5

Open the box — three operations

Purification — in 2 bar · top 50 °C, 2 bar · bottom 80 °C, 2 bar

The little P and T boxes are the whole reason fluid mechanics and thermodynamics are on your timetable

Step 5 of 5 · major equipment placement

Only now does it become a plant

Reactor 95 °C, 10 bar · Phase Separation 50 °C, 10 bar · Purification in 2 bar, top 50 °C, bottom 80 °C

Same three boxes as the slide before — pumps, exchangers, a packed bed, a flash drum and a column, and the plant is real

Year 4 the capstone, term by term

Year 4 is designing a real plant

Semester 1 · 2105415 Chemical Process Design I · 4(2-6-4)

Process synthesis

  • Pick the reaction, set feed and product
  • Build the process model in simulation software
  • Plant-wide simulation

Groups of three · 17 weeks · a live industrial brief (sustainable aviation fuel, CO2 utilisation)

PI 2.3PI 3.2PI 4.3PI 5.2PI 6.1PI 7.3PI 8.2
Semester 2 · 2105416 Chemical Process Design II · 4(2-6-4)

Equipment, energy, money, planet

  • Size and cost the major equipment
  • Heat-exchanger network and energy recovery
  • Plant layout, economics, and a life-cycle assessment in week 14

Assessed in front of a panel from industry

PI 2.3PI 3.2PI 5.1PI 5.2PI 6.2PI 7.3PI 7.4PI 8.1PI 8.2PI 10.1

Prerequisite: Design II follows Design I · the senior project 2105417 → 2105418 runs beside them

Direct assessment · DA1 embedded questions

Your exam is the measurement

Two questions from one real paper — every part carries the indicator it measures

Question 1 · distillation column
1.1PI 1.47 marksFlows and propane fractions in all three streams
1.2PI 3.18 marksRecommend the operating pressure and condenser type
1.3PI 1.57 marksFeed temperature, if feed pressure equals column pressure
1.4PI 3.110 marksReflux rate as a multiple of minimum reflux
Question 2 · heat exchanger
PI 1.4 PI 2.1 30 marks

Decide whether an existing double-pipe exchanger can transfer heat from hot ethanol to cooling water.

  • Ethanol 0.5 kg/s, 1 bar · 70 °C in, 40 °C out
  • Water 1 bar · 30 °C in, 50 °C out wanted
  • Inner pipe 25 mm ID, 2 mm wall · annulus 40 mm ID · 72 m long · k = 16.25 W/m·K
  • Nusselt correlations given for laminar, transition and turbulent flow

Nobody sat an extra test — your marks on 1.1 and on question 2 are what the program reports for PI 1.4
